newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Eskom mark bond on hold due lack fx cover.
newsitem.headline: Eskom mark bond on hold due lack fx cover.

text.p: South African electricity utility Eskom has put on indefinite hold plans to launch a 200 million mark five-year Eurobond because of the government's reluctance to provide forward foreign exchange cover.
Treasury general manager Johan van de Berg told Reuters on thursday that without long-term cover from the central Reserve Bank the issue would not be viable.

"We are not comfortable at this stage to enter into a five-year liability denominated in Deutschmarks without forward cover. The currency risk is just not according to our appetite right now," he said.

"If we don't get the long-term cover from the government and we have to source that cover from the commercial banking sector, then we would probably end up paying a premium of 150 basis points over local capital market rates."

Finance Minister Trevor Manuel announced last year that the government was reviewing the whole issue of providing long-term forward foreign exchange cover in a bid to reduce the central bank's exposure to potentially huge losses.

The Reserve Bank has traditionally provided such cover, notably to parastatals like Eskom, because of the lack of a commercial alterative -- resulting in huge losses on the Bank's forward book. Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said last August that the Bank's net oversold foreign exchange position stood at $15 billion at that stage.

Van den Berg said the finance department had indicated that in future forward cover would be provided only on an exceptional basis and not as a general rule. But no official notice of any change had been announced.

"We have requested the department of finance for a final decision on this and we have not heard anything from them yet. Our plans for the Deutschmark issue are dependent on the answer we get," he said.
"We expect a decision within the next two weeks to one month from now."
Van den Berg said Eskom had been anticipating that the mark Eurobond would be issued in March when another five-year 300 million mark issue matures.
That timing would have been good, since Eskom might have caught same of the same investor base for the new issue, but it was not critical. "Our funding requirement is very small," he said.
Eskom already took a decision late last year to delay the mark issue due to the weakness of the rand and the lack of interest in German capital markets for South African debt at that time.
